title: Tool-use loop
acceptance: Given a scripted model, then tools run in order, results are fed back, and the loop ends when a ruling is submitted.
Given an invalid ruling, then the validation error is returned and the model may retry.
Given no decision within the step budget, then a clear error is raised.
evidence: PR 1: loop tests with a scripted model.

title: Provider adapters
status: Implemented, not verified end to end
acceptance: Given Anthropic or OpenAI, then tool calls and tool results are encoded in each provider's format.
evidence: manual: PR 3, scripted Anthropic responses in Chrome exercised two model calls with tool results appended. OpenAI not exercised.

title: Duplicate detection
acceptance: Given an issue and the open pool, then similar issues are ranked and unrelated ones excluded.

title: Ruling validation
acceptance: Given model output, then kind, priority, summary and reply are required, confidence is clamped, and unknown values are rejected, duplicate_of must be a loaded open issue, and summary and reply are length-limited.
Given issue text or file contents, then they reach the model delimited as untrusted data, and read_repo_file accepts only plain relative paths (no dot segments, encoded or not).

title: Auditable ledger and ruling view
acceptance: Given a run, then each completed tool call appears on a timeline and the ruling shows kind, priority, labels, duplicate, missing information and a copyable reply.
evidence: manual: PR 3, rendered in Chrome with a scripted model.

title: Keyboard, batch and export
acceptance: Given the list, then J/K move, R rules, B triages the next five in sequence, C copies the reply, and all rulings export as JSON.
Given a run in progress, when R, B or Enter is pressed, then no second run starts.
Given a focused button or link, when Enter is pressed, then the control activates natively and the shortcut does not fire.
evidence: manual: PR 4, verified against zod with a scripted model: five calls, five priority marks, export shown.

title: Provider key kept in the session by default
acceptance: Given a provider key, then it is kept in sessionStorage for the tab by default, kept on the device only when the user ticks "Remember on this device", and removable with "Clear key"; the provider choice persists.
evidence: In Chrome with an invalid test key the key stayed in sessionStorage (SEC-002).

title: Content Security Policy on the static export
acceptance: Given the Pages export, then every page carries a Content-Security-Policy meta tag that allows scripts only from the site and from the hashes of its inline scripts, and connections only to the site, api.anthropic.com, api.openai.com, api.github.com and raw.githubusercontent.com.
evidence: Hash and policy tests; published site checked in Chrome after deploy (SEC-001).

title: Product analytics, off without a key
status: Implemented, not verified end to end
acceptance: Given no NEXT_PUBLIC_POSTHOG_KEY when the web app is built, then neither the Vercel build nor the Pages export contains analytics code (nothing in the client output mentions PostHog), and the browser downloads no analytics script and makes no analytics request.
Given no POSTHOG_KEY when the bot runs, then the analytics SDK is not loaded and nothing is sent.

Given a key, then the web app sends $pageview and triage_requested (repo: the public owner/name), and the bot sends issue_triaged (repo, labels_applied, model, latency_ms, outcome) and webhook_rejected (reason); the bot flushes its events before the process exits.
Given any event, then it carries app (triage-desk) and surface (web or bot), its name is object_verb and its properties are snake_case.

Given any event, then it contains only counts, booleans, durations in milliseconds, enumerations and the public repository name; never an issue title, body, comment, username, provider key, token or ruling text.
Given the web app, then analytics uses no cookies or browser storage, builds no person profiles, does not autocapture or record sessions, and respects Do Not Track.

Given the Vercel deployment, then events go through the same-origin /ingest path; given the Pages export, then its content security policy allows the PostHog hosts in script-src and connect-src only when NEXT_PUBLIC_POSTHOG_HOST is set at deploy.

Given no NEXT_PUBLIC_POSTHOG_KEY on the Vercel deployment, then the app registers no /ingest route at all, so it forwards nothing to PostHog; the proxy is a server-side route and exists only when a key is set.
evidence: manual: No key: Vercel build and Pages export built from clean trees, `grep -rli posthog .next/static out` empty, and in headless Chromium the Vercel build made no analytics request, wrote no cookie or storage and printed nothing to the console. Control build with a key emits the 315 KB SDK chunk, lazily. With a fake key in Chromium (requests to /ingest stubbed): only same-origin /ingest requests, no cookies or storage from analytics, `$pageview` carried origin and path, `triage_requested` carried only `repo`, and a planted issue title, body, username and API key appeared in no payload. `/ingest` rewrites checked against the live host (asset 200 through rule 1, trailing-slash POST not redirected); with no key the config registers no `/ingest` rewrite (asserted by calling its `rewrites()`), so the app is not a relay. Bot run against a real issue in dry run: without a key `posthog-node` is never resolved and nothing is sent; with a key one `issue_triaged` is flushed before exit, also on the invalid-event and failure paths (requests intercepted). Not exercised: delivery to a PostHog project with a real token.
